name: Pacific Ocean
alt: A world map with a huge highlighted body of water spanning nearly half the globe.
facts: This is the biggest ocean — it's bigger than all the continents put together!
It's so wide that it touches Asia, Australia, and the Americas all at once.
It's home to the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in any ocean.
It covers about a third of the entire surface of our planet.
Thousands of islands dot its waters, from tiny atolls to huge volcanic peaks.
A massive ring of volcanoes and earthquake zones, sometimes called the "Ring of Fire," surrounds much of it.
Many coral reefs, including some of the most colorful in the world, grow in its warm western waters.
Strong currents here can carry drifting objects thousands of miles from where they started.

name: Atlantic Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted body of water shaped like a long 'S', sitting between two groups of landmasses.
facts: This ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.
It's the second largest ocean in the world, after the Pacific.
Ships and planes have crossed it for centuries, making it one of the most traveled oceans.
A powerful warm current flows through it and even warms parts of nearby coastlines.
A long underwater mountain range runs down the middle of its floor, splitting it almost in half.
Many famous shipwrecks rest at the bottom of this ocean, hidden far below the surface.
Hurricanes that hit the eastern coasts of the Americas often form over its warm waters.
Sailors once called crossing it the "crossing of the pond," since it became such a common journey.

name: Indian Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted body of water bordered by land on three sides, north of the icy southern waters.
facts: This is the warmest ocean in the world.
It's the third largest ocean, named after the country of India along its coast.
Unlike most oceans, it's bordered by land on three sides instead of two.
Monsoon winds blow across it, shifting direction with the seasons and shaping weather for nearby lands.
It's home to thousands of coral islands, including low-lying atolls just a few feet above the waves.
Ancient traders used its winds to sail back and forth between Africa, Arabia, and Asia for thousands of years.
A huge underwater plateau lies hidden beneath its surface, believed by scientists to be part of a sunken landmass.
Many of the world's busiest shipping routes for oil and goods cross through its waters.

name: Arctic Ocean
alt: A world map with a small highlighted body of water at the very top of the globe, mostly covered in ice.
facts: This is the smallest and coldest ocean, and parts of it are covered in ice.
It sits at the very top of the globe, around the North Pole.
Much of it freezes over in winter, and animals like polar bears hunt right on the ice.
Sea ice here can be several feet thick, and explorers once traveled across it by sled.
The sun doesn't set for weeks at a time near its center during the summer months.
It's the shallowest of the world's major oceans, with much of its floor closer to the surface than the others.
Narwhals and beluga whales swim beneath its icy surface, well adapted to the frigid water.
It's less salty than other oceans because so many rivers from nearby continents flow into it.

name: Southern Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted ring of water encircling the icy landmass at the very bottom of the globe.
facts: This ocean surrounds Antarctica and is home to many penguins and whales.
It's the newest ocean to be officially recognized by name.
Strong winds and currents circle all the way around Antarctica here, uninterrupted by any other land.
Its icy waters are home to some of the largest creatures on Earth, including blue whales.
Massive icebergs, some as big as small towns, drift through it after breaking off the ice nearby.
It has no countries bordering it directly — only the icy continent it surrounds.
Scientists only agreed on its official boundaries fairly recently, after long debate.
Albatrosses can glide above its rough waves for thousands of miles without ever touching land.
